site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

run_plan.goal: Evaluate the UX of the Tessera documentation site, focusing on information architecture, navigation consistency, and the usability of technical reference pages (SQL/Functions) across desktop and mobile viewports.
run_plan.summary: The run will start at the homepage to validate global navigation and theme/version controls. It will then traverse the primary 'Reference' flow, testing the deep-linking TOC and specific function pages (`DATE_TRUNC`, `JSON_EXTRACT`) for content layout and readability. Finally, it will verify SQL syntax pages and repeat critical checks on mobile to address known tap-target risks.
assumptions: The 'Tutorials', 'Download', and 'GitHub' links in the header are placeholders (#) or external, so exploration will focus on internal docs/reference pages.
The left-hand TOC on reference pages is interactive (expand/collapse) as indicated by the prescan description.
The version switcher and theme toggle persist across all internal pages.
risk_hotspots: Global Header: Version switcher lacks accessible labels; multiple tap targets < 44px height.
Reference Page: Deep nested TOC navigation and sticky behavior on scroll.
Function Pages: Code block readability and 'Version History' collapsible panel interaction.
Mobile Viewport: High density of small tap targets in the header and TOC.

phases.title: Homepage & Global Controls
phases.objective: Validate entry point clarity, global navigation persistence, and utility controls (Search, Theme, Version).
key_checks: Verify 'Get Started' and 'View Reference' CTAs lead to expected destinations.
Toggle Dark/Light theme and observe visual state change and persistence.
Interact with Version Switcher (v2.4/v2.3/etc) to check dropdown behavior.
Trigger Command-K Search modal to verify overlay and input focus.
exit_criteria: Theme toggle visually updates the UI.
Search modal opens and accepts input.
All main nav links are clickable.

phases.title: Reference Architecture & Navigation
phases.objective: Assess the usability of the three-column reference layout and deep-linking TOC.
key_checks: Expand/Collapse nodes in the left-hand TOC (e.g., Functions > Aggregate).
Click a popular link (e.g., 'DATE_TRUNC') to test deep linking.
Scroll the center content pane to verify if the right-hand 'On this page' outline updates active state.
Check responsiveness of the three-column layout when resizing window.
exit_criteria: TOC nodes expand/collapse without layout shift errors.
Internal links navigate correctly to specific function pages.
Right-hand outline highlights current section on scroll.

phases.title: Technical Content & Function Details
phases.objective: Critique the presentation of complex technical data (signatures, params, examples) on specific function pages.
key_checks: Validate code block syntax highlighting and copy-to-clipboard functionality (if present).
Interact with 'Version History' collapsible panel at the bottom of the page.
Verify table readability for 'Parameters' and 'Return Value' sections.
Check breadcrumb navigation ('> FUNCTIONS > DATE / TIME') for correct hierarchy and clickability.
exit_criteria: Code blocks are legible and distinct from body text.
Version history panel toggles open/closed smoothly.

phases.title: SQL Syntax & Data Types
phases.objective: Ensure consistent styling and navigation for broader concept pages compared to specific function pages.
key_checks: Review 'SELECT' statement syntax diagram/table for horizontal overflow handling.
Check 'Data Types' table for responsive behavior (stacking vs scrolling).
Verify that 'Edit this page on GitHub' links are present and consistent.
Test back-navigation to Reference home via sidebar or breadcrumbs.
exit_criteria: Wide tables/code blocks do not break mobile layout (horizontal scroll available).
Navigation back to parent categories works intuitively.

phases.title: Mobile Validation & Accessibility
phases.objective: Re-run critical flows on mobile viewport to address prescan warnings regarding tap targets and layout.
key_checks: Verify header hamburger menu (if applicable) or horizontal scroll behavior for nav links.
Attempt to tap small header controls (Theme, Version) to assess error rate/usability.
Check if the left-hand TOC collapses into a drawer or remains visible on narrow screens.
Validate font sizes for code blocks and parameter tables on mobile.
exit_criteria: No critical layout breakage on mobile viewport.
Identification of specific 'fat finger' issues in the header and TOC.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise Theme Toggle, Version Switcher, Search Modal, TOC Expand/Collapse, Collapsible Panels.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1, 2, and 3 checks on mobile viewport (width < 768px).

notes: Prescan indicates missing aria-labels on the version switcher; note this in accessibility findings.
Many header tap targets are reported < 44px; prioritize observing actual user difficulty here during mobile phase.
The 'Tutorials' and 'Download' links appear to be stubs (#); do not spend time debugging broken links there unless they unexpectedly navigate.

observation.title: DATE_TRUNC — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub DATE_TRUNC Truncate a timestamp to the precision specified by unit, returning a TIMESTAMP at the start of that period. DATE_TRUNC is commonly used in analytical queries to bucket timestamps by week, day, or hour for aggregation. Signature DATE_TRUNC(unit TEXT, timestamp TIMESTAMP) → TIMESTAMP Parameters Name Type Required Description unit TEXT required Truncation unit. One of: microsecond, millisecond, second, minute, hour, day, week, month, quarter, year, decade, century. timestamp TIMESTAMP required The input timestamp. Timezone is preserved. Return value A TIMESTAMP value at the start of the period containing the input. The return preserves the timezone of the input. Examples 1. Truncate to day Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('day', '2026-05-12 14:35:22'::TIMESTAMP) AS day_start; Result day_start 2026-05-12 00:00:00 2. Bucket events by hour for aggregation Combine DATE_TRUNC with GROUP BY to compute rolled-up metrics. Copy SELECT DATE_TRUNC('hour', created_at) AS hour_bucket, COUNT(*) AS events, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-12' GROUP BY hour_bucket ORDER BY hour_bucket; Result hour_bucket events revenue 2026-05-12 00:00:00 142 38,420 2026-05-12 01:00:00 89 22,180 2026-05-12 02:00:00 61 14,902 3. Nested with EXTRACT for weekday rollups Copy SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE_TRUNC('day', created_at)) AS dow, COUNT(*) AS n FROM telemetry_samples GROUP BY dow ORDER BY dow; Result dow n 0 8420 1 12940 2 13580 Errors Common errors: invalid_unit: passing a unit string Tessera does not recognise (e.g. 'fortnight') raises this error. null_input: returns NULL if either argument is NULL. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Improved performance for hour and minute truncation by ~28% via SIMD vectorization. v2.3Fixed a timezone bug where DST transitions could shift the result by 1 hour for week truncation. v2.1Added the 'microsecond' unit. v1.0Added in initial release. observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub REGEXP_MATCH Test whether a string matches a regular expression using the RE2 syntax. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Pattern cache size raised from 256 to 1024 entries. v2.0Switched regex engine from PCRE to RE2 for predictable execution time. Some lookbehinds no longer supported. v1.5Added flags parameter. v1.0Added in initial release. Number all rows by created_at Copy SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY created_at) AS rn FROM orders; Result id rn ord_001 1 ord_002 2 ord_003 3 2. observation.title: SELECT statement — Tessera
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array SELECT statement SELECT is the workhorse of Tessera. Its clauses are evaluated in a fixed order even though they may be written in any order in the source text. Syntax SELECT [DISTINCT] expression FROM source [WHERE] predicate [GROUP BY] expression [HAVING] predicate [ORDER BY] expression [LIMIT] n [OFFSET] n WITH Common table expressions for readability and recursion. Copy WITH recent AS ( SELECT id, amount_cents FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-05-01' ) SELECT SUM(amount_cents) FROM recent; FROM Sources can be tables, subqueries, table-valued functions, or external file readers. Copy SELECT * FROM read_parquet('s3://bucket/orders/*.parquet'); WHERE Row-level filter applied before grouping. Supports any expression returning BOOLEAN. GROUP BY Groups rows by the listed expressions. SELECT items must be aggregates or referenced in GROUP BY. HAVING Post-grouping filter, evaluated after aggregates compute. ORDER BY Sorts the final result. Supports ASC / DESC and NULLS FIRST / LAST. LIMIT and OFFSET Restricts the row count. OFFSET can be expensive on large result sets — prefer cursor pagination. Performance tip. Push column projection and filters into your storage layer when reading from Parquet — Tessera's read_parquet applies predicate pushdown automatically when supported. Examples Copy -- Top spenders this quarter SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount_cents) AS total FROM orders WHERE created_at >= '2026-04-01' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount_cents) > 100000 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 20; ON THIS PAGE Syntax WITH FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY LIMIT Examples © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.

observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 › SCHEMAS › TABLES › VIEWS › INDEXES › FUNCTIONS AGGREGATE SUM AVG COUNT MIN MAX ARRAY_AGG STRING LENGTH SUBSTR REPLACE REGEXP_MATCH LOWER UPPER NUMERIC ROUND FLOOR CEIL ABS POWER DATE / TIME NOW DATE_TRUNC EXTRACT DATE_ADD JSON JSON_EXTRACT JSON_VALID JSON_AGG WINDOW ROW_NUMBER RANK LAG LEAD › OPERATORS CATEGORIES Arithmetic Comparison Logical String JSON Array 📝 Edit this page on GitHub REGEXP_MATCH Test whether a string matches a regular expression using the RE2 syntax. REGEXP_MATCH evaluates to TRUE when pattern matches anywhere in the input string. Anchor with ^ and $ for full-string matches. Signature REGEXP_MATCH(string TEXT, pattern TEXT [, flags TEXT]) → BOOLEAN Parameters Name Type Required Description string TEXT required The string to test. pattern TEXT required A RE2-compatible regular expression. flags TEXT optional Optional flags: 'i' case-insensitive, 's' dotall, 'm' multiline. Return value TRUE if the pattern matches anywhere in the string, FALSE otherwise. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL. Examples 1. Simple match Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('service-12', '^service-\d+$'); Result regexp_match true 2. Case insensitive match with flag Copy SELECT REGEXP_MATCH('ABC123', '^abc', 'i'); Result regexp_match true 3. Filter rows matching pattern Copy SELECT email FROM customers WHERE REGEXP_MATCH(email, '^.+@example\.(com|org)$'); Result email ana@example.com julien@example.org nora@example.com Errors Common errors: invalid_regex: malformed pattern (unbalanced parens, invalid escape). regex_timeout: pattern took longer than 100ms to evaluate. Version history 4 entries ▼ v2.4Pattern cache size raised from 256 to 1024 entries. v2.0Switched regex engine from PCRE to RE2 for predictable execution time. observation.title: Tessera — The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics.
observation.visible_text: Tessera Docs Reference Tutorials Download GitHub v2.4 (latest) v2.3 v2.2 v2.1 ⌘ K Search 🌓 v2.4 · 2026-04 release The embeddable SQL engine for fast local analytics. Tessera runs in your process, reads Parquet and CSV directly, and ships SIMD-optimized vector kernels for sub-millisecond aggregation over millions of rows. Get started → View reference SELECT SELECT region, SUM(amount_cents) AS revenue FROM read_parquet('orders/*.parquet') WHERE created_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC; Quick start 1 Install Drop-in single-file build for Linux, macOS, Windows. No service to run. 2 Connect Open a file-backed or in-memory database with one line in your language of choice. 3 Your first query Run analytical queries directly on Parquet, CSV, and Arrow data. Documentation Architecture Storage, vectorized execution, and query planning. SQL Syntax Statements, expressions, and railroad diagrams. Functions Scalar, aggregate, window, and string functions. Data Types Native and extended types with storage details. Storage Page format, WAL, snapshots, and replication. Extensions Geospatial, JSON, vector search, and full-text. © 2026 Tessera Foundation · Local demo for UXBench. Fictional product, not a real company.
